overview: Build a ship out of ordinary blocks, put a helm on it, christen it with a bottle and sail the whole thing away as one vessel.

1.3.5: Mod Menu's Donate button leads to sponsoring the author on GitHub. Nothing in play changes.
1.3.4: Works with Pandorical as old as 15.13.0. Before 15.18 a ship's hold takes the sea while she sails, and before 15.17 the Ship menu leaves out Share and Unshare: /ship-lock share and /ship-lock unshare still do it.
1.3.3: A mod menu icon of a two-masted ship under sail.
1.3.2: Ships are faster at the top end: a held throttle on open water now builds to about 16 blocks a second instead of 9, in the same sixteen seconds or so. Harbour speed and handling are unchanged.
A pile on the deck, of snow or anything stacked in layers the way snow is, sails with the ship instead of being left hanging in the air where she was moored.
Docking clears grass, snow or a stray pile out of the way of the ship's own blocks, as she does at sea, instead of handing one of her blocks back as an item.
1.3.1: A ship floating clear of a reef sails off it: coral reaching up to just under the keel no longer counts as part of her.
1.3.0: A ship's hold stays dry while she sails: below the waterline is air, not sea, so you walk it, see it clearly and don't drown in it.
An open boat's hull keeps the water out too, as long as her sides stand above it, and what was dry at sea is still dry when she docks.
1.2.1: A Ship action menu: who's crew, lock, unlock, and sharing with or taking back from players picked by face.
1.2.0: A ship at sea is still a working ship: her doors, trapdoors and gates swing, her chests, barrels and shulker boxes open, and her crafting table, anvil, enchanting table, loom and the rest work at sea.
Furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces and brewing stands keep going while she sails, and hoppers keep feeding them.
Bells ring and note blocks play from the deck.
A locked chest stays locked at sea and is still locked, to the same owner, wherever she docks.
A loot chest aboard opens as each player's own copy, at sea as ashore.
Ladders and vines climb at sea.
Clicking blocks on a ship at sea needs Pandorical 15.13 on the client.
1.1.1: A block added to a ship keeps the way it was laid when the ship docks again.
Stairs, logs and anything else with a facing came back turned by the ship's own heading.
A ship that had never been turned was unaffected, which is why it took a while to show.
1.1.0: Ships lock the way chests do. /ship-lock makes the ship you are standing on yours.
Share lets a crew take the helm; anyone else is kept off it and off its blocks.
Ships christened before this stay open until somebody locks them.
A deck no longer keeps a hole you fall through.
Docking a grown ship hands a blocked-out block back once rather than twice.
A ship with part of itself in an unloaded chunk waits instead of sailing without that half.
1.0.1: Everything aboard turns about the same point, so a ship is drawn where it actually is.
A quarter turn no longer leaves a seat hanging a block off the deck.
Decks can be walked on while the ship is under way.
Coral, fans, pickles and loose terrain give way to a hull, so reefs can be threaded.
1.0.0: Build any structure, set a helm in it, and christen it with a heart of the sea in a bottle.
A plain helm carries a hundred blocks; Tonnage raises it to four hundred, a thousand, two thousand.
A fisherman sells the planks, the helm, the bottle and both recipes.
Nothing else in the game hints that a ship is possible at all.
